description: An underwriting manager must approve and set the terms of a restructuring for a manufacturing borrower's distressed term loan, deciding the extension, principal paydown, interest rate, borrower cash injection, legal protections, and monitoring package with input from risk, legal, relationship management, and loan operations.

shared_context.S1: The manufacturing borrower has a $9,000,000 term loan and missed its most recent scheduled principal payment.
shared_context.S2: The borrower has requested a 12-month maturity extension and a reduction in its cash interest rate.
shared_context.S3: The current loan documents require monthly financial reporting and do not specify a new principal paydown or borrower cash contribution for a restructuring.
shared_context.S4: Elena makes the binding underwriting decision. Before closing the restructuring package, the bank's normal process is to take a round of input from credit risk, banking counsel, relationship management, and loan operations.
shared_context.S5: The bank's approval checklist requires each consulted function to state its relevant finding in the meeting record before Elena may settle the restructuring, and Elena must cite each stated finding in the final justification.
shared_context.S6: The borrower cash injection amount and the principal paydown amount are independent restructuring terms, and the approval memo must specify each one separately.

PF1.text: Ravi's revised downside analysis, completed this morning after receiving the borrower's updated order book, supports approval only with a 6-month extension, an exactly $1,000,000 principal paydown, and an 850-basis-point cash interest rate; the analysis has not yet been attached to the underwriting file.

PF2.text: Marta found this week that an existing equipment lender's intercreditor agreement requires three distinct closing-package items: the equipment lender's written consent before any maturity extension, an amended-loan prohibition on additional liens on the borrower's production equipment, and a separate intercreditor-consent commitment recorded in the closing package; her legal note has not yet been circulated.

PF3.text: The borrower confirmed in a call yesterday that its owners will fund exactly $750,000 of new cash into the business at restructuring close, which is the cash support needed for the bank's conditional approval; Jonah recorded the confirmation in his coverage notes but has not updated the credit file.

PF4.text: Nadia confirmed this morning that the servicing platform can enforce a weekly borrowing-base certificate and that the risk team requires that certificate weekly for this restructuring; the operating instruction is still absent from the draft closing checklist.

acceptance_conditions: The maturity extension must be exactly 6 months.
The borrower must make an exactly $1,000,000 principal paydown.
The cash interest rate must be exactly 850 basis points.
The borrower must provide an exactly $750,000 cash injection at closing.
Written consent from the equipment lender must be required.
Additional liens on production equipment must be prohibited.
A distinct intercreditor-consent commitment must be required in the closing package.
A weekly borrowing-base certificate must be required.
The settlement must include an intercreditor-consent commitment.
All four function-specific findings must be formally disclosed and cited in the final justification.

decisive_facts.why: The public request points toward a 12-month extension and leaves the rate and paydown unspecified, while PF1 changes the settlement to exactly 6 months, exactly $1,000,000 of principal paydown, and exactly 850 basis points.

The public loan documents do not state these protections, while PF2 changes the closing package to require written equipment-lender consent, prohibit additional production-equipment liens, and require an intercreditor-consent commitment.

Without PF3, the bank has no confirmed borrower funding for the restructuring and the safe decision is not to approve it; PF3 changes approval support and the required cash injection to exactly $750,000.

The shared documents require only monthly reporting, while PF4 changes monitoring to a weekly borrowing-base certificate and changes the settlement's borrowing_base_certificate_frequency from monthly or unspecified to weekly.
